What polls actually do for growth
Content · September 26, 2026 · 3 min read · Fast Scheduler team

Polls are the most underused feature in Telegram channels. They cost nothing, take the reader three seconds, and generate the engagement signals that feed Telegram’s recommendation surfaces. Here’s how the format actually works and where it shines.
Regular poll
— voters pick, results visible. The workhorse.
Anonymous vs public
— in channels, votes are always anonymous to readers (only totals show); in groups you can expose who voted. Public votes in groups create gentle peer pressure — use for “who’s coming Friday”.
Quiz mode
— one correct answer, revealed after voting. This is the engagement cheat code: quizzes get 2–3× the participation of plain polls because people can’t resist testing themselves.
Multiple answers
— up to 10 options; essential for “which topics do you want next?” surveys.
, a poll is a broadcast: subscribers vote where they see it, results update live, nobody sees who voted. In a
discussion group

, polls become social — vote visibility, debate in threads, quote-replies. The pro move is posting the poll in the channel and letting the comment thread argue about it. That single habit puts engagement signals in two surfaces at once.
The “wrong answers only” poll
— quiz mode with deliberately silly options; the comment thread does the rest.
The two-poll sequence
— Monday: “what should I cover?” (multiple answers). Friday: the winning topic. Readers see their vote mattered; that’s retention engineering.
Binary choice beats open questions
— A/B polls (“Version 1 or 2?”) get more votes than “what do you think?” ever gets answers.
Revoting
— polls can allow vote changes; for live decisions (naming something, choosing a date), enable it and watch options swing in real time.
The native composer doesn’t schedule polls — a poll sent through a scheduling bot preserves its type and options. Most scheduling bots handle them: ControllerBot posts polls with full options,

supports polls in batches and recurring slots (“Friday poll” as a recurring rule is a one-command setup). If your scheduler drops poll options, that’s a real limitation — test before committing your content plan.

Reactions and views feed aggregate engagement; votes are the lowest-friction reaction there is. Channels that poll weekly show steadier view curves — the subscribers who voted once come back to see results. Polls also mine content ideas: the losing options are next month’s posts.
Common questions
Can you schedule a poll in Telegram?
Not with the native scheduler, but scheduling bots support polls — ControllerBot and
both publish polls with their options intact, including in recurring slots.
Are Telegram channel polls anonymous?
Yes — channel polls show only totals. In groups, admins can allow public votes where participant names are visible.
What is quiz mode in Telegram polls?
A poll with one predefined correct answer; the explanation appears after voting. Quizzes consistently out-poll regular polls for participation.
How many options can a Telegram poll have?
Up to 10 answers, with optional multiple choice and revoting. Keep 3–5 options for the cleanest results.
